newsitem.title: UK: Relatives of accused British nurses head to Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Relatives of accused British nurses head to Saudi.

text.p: Relatives of the two British nurses on trial for murder in Saudi Arabia headed to the oil-rich state on Friday to lend them moral support.
An official at Roger Pannone, the law firm representing the two women, said the relatives were flying out on Friday morning but that no statements were expected until late next week.
Deborah Parry, 41, and Lucille McLaughlan, 31, are accused of murdering Australian nurse Yvonne Gilford at a medical centre in Dhahran last December.
Both nurses deny the murder but if convicted they could face public beheading by the sword.
Alternatively, under Saudi law, the Gilford family could spare their lives by accepting financial compensation known as blood money.
The two women have written a personal letter to the Gilford family and the Saudi court has adjourned the case for three weeks to give the Gilford family time to think.
Parry and McLaughlan, who have complained of ill-treatment after their arrest, have yet to give evidence in court.
Defence lawyers have given the court several pages of evidence and say that the two women were put under strong pyschological pressure to admit to the crime.
Stephen Jakobi of the Fair Trials Abroad organisation said the judicial proceedings contained "a fatal flaw" and questioned the tactics employed by Saudi police to obtain the women's confessions.
"Death sentences may be inflicted on the innocent unless all tainted police evidence is thrown out as soon as the court resumes to begin hearing the evidence in mid-June," Jakobi said in a statement.
The younger nurse, Scots-born McLaughlan, has also written from jail to a friend in her home city of Dundee protesting her innocence.
"What upsets me is that Yvonne was my friend, a kind, caring lady who looked after me when I first came to Saudi," she wrote. "For people to say I did this to her makes me very angry."
